newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Harried Australia dlr cornered near key support.
newsitem.headline: Harried Australia dlr cornered near key support.

text.p: The Australian dollar was brought to bay just above key support at the midsession having found only transient relief in the lack of a rate cut this morning.

Dealers said bids were expected to be sizeable at the year-low and major chart level of US$0.7550, but bears looked to have the advantage for the moment having crushed all attempts to rally past US$0.7630 resistance on Wednesday.

Signs of Japanese selling -- dealers reported talk a Tokyo bank was looking to offload around A$500 million -- worried bulls as Japanese investors had been helpfully quiet recently compared to the aggressive dumping seen from U.S. houses.
By 12.30 pm (0230 GMT) the dollar had been hounded to US$0.7565/75 from US$0.7690/95 late here Wednesday and a brief peak of US$0.7630.
Traders said stops were believed to be building below US$0.7550 and a break could well trigger a burst of distressed selling down to 75 cents.

It would also be very bearish from a technical viewpoint with analysts seeing US$0.7450 as a first target and potential for the downtrend to even reach the 1996 low of 73 cents. A push atop US$0.7630 was needed to relieve the immediate pressure and a reversal would only come with the seizure of US$0.7770.
On the crosses the currency slipped to 87.80/90 yen from 88.40/50 late Wednesday as AUD/yen offers came out of Tokyo and to 57.7 in trade weighted terms from 57.9.

The dollar did try to bounce after the Reserve Bank stayed silent at its morning market operation, again confounding speculation of an imminent easing, but the rally barely reached US$0.7585 before fresh selling emerged.

Some bulls were hoping today's inaction by the RBA meant rates were on hold until its next board meeting in July but conceded it was impossible for the market to relax given the bank had surprised it with three of the last four cuts.
Dealers were hoping for some guidance on policy by RBA governor Ian Macfarlane who addresses a Westpac conference in London tonight at around 01.50 am our time.
No title for the speech was known but it was thought to be about economic developments in Australia, so some inkling of the bank's policy thinking may emerge.

The March quarter GDP report out Wednesday provided plenty for both the steady and easing camps and the market would have to wait for May employment data next Thursday for another economic signpost on policy.
